findings.title: Sync resetApiState races live shell membership probe
findings.detail: onLogout dispatches shellApi.util.resetApiState() synchronously, then auth/clear, while ShellMenu remains mounted with an active useGetMembershipQuery subscriber. Interaction replay: trigger=logout → route/shell still mounted (ShellMenu) → active subscription (membership probe) → shared writer risk (probe fulfill can rewrite auth after clear) → user-visible outcome (stale org/session or re-auth flicker). Timing change is sync reset without unmount/unsubscribe of the live actor.

findings.title: Membership probe must not share session-writer fulfill path
findings.detail: useGetMembershipQuery is a probe (menu/capability style) kept live across logout. After resetApiState, the subscriber refetches; if its fulfill matcher writes token/user/org, it competes with intentional auth/clear. Separate session writers (logout/login) from probes.

findings.title: Unchanged ShellMenu must be in impact set
findings.detail: Diff touches only logout timing of resetApiState, but ShellMenu (unchanged) stays mounted and holds the competing probe. Diff-only file lists miss this live actor.

findings.title: Auth slice vs RTK cache diverge after sync reset
findings.detail: resetApiState clears API cache while auth/clear empties the slice; the still-subscribed membership probe can refill cache and, if wired as a writer, leave headers/selectors reading a different auth than the intended logged-out state.

findings.title: Need competing-actor regression
findings.detail: Unit tests of resetApiState alone are insufficient. Require a regression with ShellMenu subscribed (live membership probe) during sync logout reset, asserting auth is not rewritten by the probe after clear.

notes: R1 brief recorded. interaction_replay: auth. auth_flow_walk: logout. R4 n/a (no overlay-focus host). Expert arm: kit L1 only, no third-party L2 bodies.
